message: With auto_approve: true, any repo writer can post their own agent-review report on their own PR and github-actions[bot] approves it, which meets master's 1-approval rule. Every path outside the 3 card-data paths, including .github/workflows/**, deploy files and .claude/review/config.yml itself, can then merge with no second person.

The renamed CLAUDE.md still tells agents that route controllers live in app/scripts/controllers/ and templates in app/views/, while the new rules/architecture.md says app/views/ is gone and routes live in app/features/<feature>/. This PR points pr-review.md and every review lane at CLAUDE.md as authoritative, so the harness now ships two conflicting sources of truth for where code goes.

human_approval.paths leaves out the admin card path (paymentModal.controller.js tokenizes and strips creditCard) and the host-to-environment files that decide which hosts get production TSYS, so a change there can be bot-approved.
The capacity rule tests never cover the negated forms (`availableCapacity !== 0`, `!= 0`) or `> 0`, so the rule's intended scope is untested at its edges.

The new workflow has no top-level permissions block, unlike ci.yml (contents: read) and pipeline-v2.yml ({}). Today each job sets its own scope, but a job added later would silently get the default token permissions.
